pass_a_gloss: He speaks of considering one’s own evil and turning again toward the person, being like a dog that eats its own vomit, similar to Lot’s wife who turned back to what the unclean spirit had drawn her toward. This saying should be applied to those who count some unworthy persons in the priesthood or in the lot, since no one among us has established the Church’s justice and freedom; it belongs either to us or to Christ, through whom He judged Himself righteous to be given over to death, and His blood was shed for her sake. Thus anyone who wishes to take charge of the Church’s households must surrender himself, seize the evil one’s collar, free those under his wickedness, and lead them into Christ’s full knowledge. Just as fire burns in wood, so anger aimed at the mind’s passions blazes in evil thoughts; where there is no double-mindedness—no divided loyalty, but either to God or to mammon—stillness arises, one overcomes the other: if God’s command prevails, the evil is subdued and makes peace with wickedness; but if one chooses both, they fall from life and lose temporary things. The lips here mean the thoughts; but whoever does not open the mind’s lips against evil, confessing to God the sins they have sown against God, but hides them, covers their heart with grief, not thinking through foolishness that they have sin in these matters; unaware of God’s good compassion; for those who endure and proclaim these things to Him, He grants crowns as if they were contending in each struggle through Him. He mocks instead of rejoicing, he has taken; for a cheerful soul, delighting in Scripture’s knowledge, rejoices in being filled; but an impure soul and false knowledge surely believes it true. Or the heart’s place, virtue and knowledge, from which a person, having been estranged, falls into wickedness and ignorance and becomes a slave of sin, doing it; since he is rational, His place: virtue. A calm mind enjoys wisdom, knowledge, song. A disturbed mind shatters in ignorance, evil, falls to incurable ruin. God is friend to us, ancestors, descendants. He said: “They left me, living water’s source, dug broken cisterns.” Christ is brother by grace. Entering brother’s house without his commands—seeking heaven’s gate—do so unhappily? Like wedding guest without garment: bound, cast out. Brother now: angel choir. Before fall, devil was angel, human. God friend. Better dwell with near true God than self-made distant devil, pretending brotherhood, to perish together. Who joins me via true knowledge surpasses who joins via nature alone. Human house: virtue. Neglect it? Falls in trial. Fig tree: God’s righteousness. Planters in self and others, grafting, eat fruit by Lord’s hand, sole just one, contend for righteousness. Those guarding his righteousness with self: he assigns righteousness—angel-justifying righteousness—in unchanging brilliance. He says, examining his own wickedness and turning back toward him, and then turning again toward him, he is like a dog eating its own vomit; just as was the wife of Lot, and she turned back toward what the unclean spirit had caused her to turn toward. This saying must be used against those who are reckoning some of the unworthy among the priesthood, or in the lot; for no one among us has established the justice and liberty of the Church; but it is either ours, or Christ’s, through which He judged Himself justified to be given over to slaughter, and His blood was poured out on her behalf; thus also every one who desires to undertake the oversight of the Church’s households must surrender himself, and seize the collar of the evil one, and liberate those under his wickedness, and bring them into the full knowledge of Christ. As fire in wood, so in evil thoughts the anger that is directed toward the passions of the mind blazes and burns; but where there is no double-mindedness, that is, no divided soul, but either to God or to mammon, stillness will come from it, the one over the other; either the commandment of God, having conquered, the evil one will be subdued, and he will make peace with wickedness; but if one chooses both, and falls out of life, and will be deprived of temporary things. The lips here he says are the thoughts; but the one who does not open the lips of the mind against the evil, confessing to God the evils which he has sown against God, but conceals them, covers his heart with grief, not thinking through folly that he has sin in these things; not knowing the God’s good compassion; for to those who thus endure and proclaim these things to Him, He awards crowns as if they were contending in each struggle through Him. He mocks, instead of rejoicing, he has taken; for a cheerful soul, delighting in the knowledge of the Scriptures, rejoices in being filled; but an impure soul, and the false knowledge, surely believes it to be true. Or the place of the heart, virtue and knowledge, from which a man, having been estranged, falls into wickedness and ignorance, and becomes a slave of sin, doing it; inasmuch as he is rational,

His place is virtue. An untroubled mind delights in varied pleasures—wisdom, knowledge, and hymnody; but a mind troubled by passion is shattered in ignorance and wickedness, and comes to a fall that is incurable and great. God is our friend and the friend of our forefathers, and of those who come after us; for he himself said, “They have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, and have hewn for themselves cisterns, broken cisterns.” Here Christ is our brother according to grace; but to enter your brother’s house without the commandments he has given us, in order to gain authority to enter his house—that is, to enter the kingdom of heaven—do not attempt it unhappily regarding these things; for such was the one who entered the wedding feast without a wedding garment; having been bound hand and foot, he was cast out of the wedding. Our brother here is the choir of angels; for according to the nature of the angels, before the transgression and fall, the devil was of the angels and of us; but God is our friend; and it is better to dwell with our true and genuine God, who is near and most closely present, than with one who has made himself far from himself a devil, as if submitting to a brother, in order to perish together with him. The one who joins with me through true knowledge is superior to the one who joins with me only through nature. The house of man is virtue; if therefore one does not attend to it with diligence, in the time of trials he falls from it. Here the fig tree is the righteousness of God, which those who plant it in themselves and in others, and who transmit it as a graft, shall eat its fruit by the hand of the Lord, the only just one, and shall contend for righteousness; and to those who guard his righteousness together with themselves, he appoints, assigning righteousness, the righteousness that also justifies angels, in the brilliant splendor of the unchanging righteousness; but whoever guards the word of the Lord, guards the Lord in his own heart as unchangeable from him; and he shall be honored not only from here on by
